correctness.rationale: The two explicitly defined 26-block systems are exhaustive among STS(13) by the published classification. Direct pair-incidence checks and two independent complete face enumerators establish 1,158 and 1,153 augmented faces. Every one of the 4,550 and 4,520 ordinary Hasse cover relations is tested for acyclicity under the specified matching; its critical-cell dimensions are (0:1,3:6,4:18) and (0:1,3:4,4:21). Independent sparse-elimination and recursive-gradient integer Morse differentials agree, with explicit determinant-+1 maximal minors in the 6x18 and 4x21 maps. Forman gives a CW structure with no one/two-cells; Hurewicz identifies four-cell attaching degrees with the checked integer matrices, so unimodular cancellation proves the two exact wedges. Direct mod-two chain ranks independently match and there are no unchecked infinite quantifiers. Reproducible code and output are included.

evidence: Forbes–Grannell–Griggs Theorem 1, 2004, p. 164, provides a universal formula for the count of k-independent sets, not a chain reduction or homotopy theorem.

originality.rationale: The relevant 2003 complete STS(13) classification (Grannell–Griggs–Knor, full relevant sections visually inspected) gives two isomorphism classes and the Pasch exchange; Forbes–Grannell–Griggs (2004, complete eight-page primary paper visually inspected) gives independent-set enumerators but not an integral homotopy classification. Its formulas can imply the two Euler characteristics and indeed describe the previously known face-count data, but they cannot imply the 2-connectivity, torsion-free Morse attaching maps and sphere-wedge homotopy types computed here. No assertion of definitive publication priority is made.

value.rationale: Order thirteen is the first Steiner triple system order possessing two nonisomorphic designs; their common line-avoiding complexes therefore constitute a small natural complete classification. The two complexes are nonpure (117 and 132 maximal five-vertex faces), so a pure-shellability shortcut is unavailable. The complete integral homotopy types distinguish the two systems beyond mere cardinality counts by proving that no lower spheres, torsion or nontrivial attaching maps persist. The known independent-set formulas alone fix Euler characteristics but not this topological structure. This resolves a motivated finite topological invariant without claiming a universal theorem for larger designs.
